{{Short description|Type of vector bundle}}
In mathematics, an '''essentially finite vector bundle''' is a particular type of [[vector bundle (algebraic geometry)|vector bundle]] defined by [[Madhav V. Nori]],<ref  name=":Nori">{{cite journal | last = Nori | first = Madhav V. | title =On the Representations of the Fundamental Group | journal = Compositio Mathematica | volume = 33 | year = 1976 | issue = 1 | pages = 29–42 | mr = 417179 | url = https://eudml.org/doc/89294}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Szamuely | first = T. | title = Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups | publisher = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics | volume = 117 | year = 2009}}</ref> as the main tool in the construction of the [[fundamental group scheme]].  Even if the definition is not intuitive there is a nice characterization that makes essentially finite vector bundles quite natural objects to study in [[algebraic geometry]]. The following notion of ''finite vector bundle'' is due to [[André Weil]] and will be needed to define essentially finite vector bundles:

==Finite vector bundles==

Let <math>X</math> be a scheme and <math>V</math> a vector bundle on <math>X</math>. For <math>f = a_0 + a_1 x + \ldots + a_n x^n  \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}[x]</math> an integral polynomial with nonnegative coefficients define
:<math>f(V) := \mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus a_0} \oplus V^{\oplus a_1} \oplus \left(V^{\otimes 2}\right)^{\oplus a_2} \oplus \ldots \oplus \left(V ^{\otimes n}\right)^{\oplus a_n} </math>
Then <math>V</math> is called '''finite''' if there are two distinct polynomials <math>f,g\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}[x]</math> for which <math>f(V)</math> is isomorphic to <math>g(V)</math>. 

==Definition==
The following two definitions coincide whenever <math>X</math> is a reduced, connected and proper scheme over a perfect field.

===According to Borne and [[Angelo Vistoli|Vistoli]]===
A vector bundle is '''essentially finite''' if it is the kernel of a morphism <math>u:F_1\to F_2</math> where <math>F_1, F_2</math> are finite vector bundles. <ref name=":BV">N. Borne, A. Vistoli ''The Nori fundamental gerbe of a fibered category'', J. Algebr. Geom. 24, No. 2, 311-353 (2015)</ref>

===The original definition of [[Madhav V. Nori|Nori]]===
A vector bundle is '''essentially finite''' if it is a [[subquotient]] of a finite vector bundle in the category of [[Nori-semistable]] vector bundles.<ref name=":Nori" />

==Properties==
* Let <math>X</math> be a reduced and connected [[Scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] over a perfect [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math>k</math> endowed with a section <math>x\in X(k)</math>.  Then a vector bundle <math>V</math> over <math>X</math> is essentially finite if and only if there exists a [[Finite morphism|finite]] <math>k</math>-[[group scheme]] <math>G</math> and a <math>G</math>-[[Torsor (algebraic geometry)|torsor]]  <math>p:P\to X</math> such that <math>V</math> becomes trivial over <math>P</math> (i.e. <math>p^*(V)\cong O_P^{\oplus r}</math>, where <math>r=rk(V)</math>).

*When <math>X</math> is a reduced, connected and proper scheme over a perfect field with a point <math>x\in X(k)</math> then the category <math>EF(X)</math> of essentially finite vector bundles provided with the usual tensor product <math>\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}</math>, the trivial object <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math> and the fiber functor <math>x^*</math> is a [[Tannakian formalism|Tannakian category]].

* The <math>k</math>-affine [[group scheme]] <math>\pi_1(X,x)</math> naturally associated to the Tannakian category <math>EF(X)</math> is called the [[fundamental group scheme]].
